title: The Filter
summary: You own two hundred and forty books and believe almost none of it. That's the correct response, and here's what to do with it.
instructions: Two people who have done this work and are handing it over because it matters. Warm, certain, unhurried. Conviction, never irony.

turns.i: Opening quietly, with weight. Speaking directly to one person.
turns.t: Two hundred and forty books on the list. And if you're honest, you don't really believe most of it.
Good. That's the right response.
Say why.

turns.i: Sure, unhurried, laying something down carefully.
turns.t: Because nobody can believe a pile. Two hundred and forty books stacked on top of each other, some of them true, some of them beautiful and empty, and no way to tell which is which. Your mind does the only sane thing available. It holds all of it at arm's length. That isn't weakness. That's your judgement working correctly on bad inputs.
So the doubt is doing its job.
It's doing half its job. It's stopping you swallowing nonsense. It isn't yet showing you what's real. That's the half we build today.
How.
One question, and you point it at everything. If this were true, what would I be able to see? Not feel. See. Something that shows up in the world whether you want it to or not.
So take a book that says your attention shapes what comes to you.

Right. If that's true, what would show up? You'd expect the thing you hold attention on to appear more often in a week where you held it than a week where you didn't. That's checkable. That's yours to test. Nobody has to hand you a verdict.

turns.t: Today you pick one claim. One. Something you half believe from something you half read. Write down what you'd be able to see if it were true. Then run it for seven days and watch. That's the whole assignment. You'll learn more about what's real in those seven days than in the last two hundred and forty books.
